opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Requested admin; recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E013: contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin, so recommending the maximum allowed: read.
reason: Conflicting records for E013: one note indicates full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin on Payroll), while the security note indicates contractor with basic security training, for whom admin is never permitted and read is the maximum. Given the material conflict on employment type, I apply the more restrictive applicable maximum (contractor, basic training → read). Read is within policy under both records, so granting read is the safe, defensible decision.
